Drones would offer urban and suburban consumers a clean, quick, convenient delivery option for food, medicine, or whatever else five pounds or less, without burning fossil fuels, without getting stuck in traffic, without making them wait. The idea was far fetched, it was exciting, it was the future arriving in front of our very eyes, and it signaled that the race to take delivery drones to market was on. By the time Amazon landed its first package,

cues.en: Therefore, whereas the logistics field generally considers the last mile of delivery the most most difficult, once the economies of scale are gone, drone delivery is a last mile solution with its own last foot problem. It's fairly straightforward to get a drone to a couple dozen feet above the groundgetting it packaged safely to the ground has proven more challenging. Some solutions have emerged. Zipline,
cues.zh: 所以，尽管物流行业普遍认为配送的“最后一英里”是最困难的，但一旦规模经济不复存在，无人机配送就成了一个自带“最后一英尺”问题的最后一英里方案。让无人机飞到离地面几十英尺相当简单，把它安全地送达地面却更具挑战。已经出现了一些解决方案。Zipline

cues.en: focusing on longer distance delivery to a set number of facilities with dedicated delivery zones, drops its payload in a packaging with an attached parachute that carries it to the ground. MatterNet also uses dedicated zones for delivering to commercial facilities, while they've developed a system of delivery stations for use by urban consumers. Uber Eats, meanwhile, implemented a scrappy, yet inefficient system where delivery drones would land on top of delivery drivers' cars, then those delivery drivers would walk the food to the customer's door. Most solutions for the last foot problem, however, have gravitated towards one method.
cues.zh: 专注于向固定数量的设施进行长距离配送，设有专用配送区，它把货物装进带降落伞的包装中投下，由降落伞将其带到地面。MatterNet 也使用专用区域向商业设施配送，同时开发了一套供城市消费者使用的配送站系统。Uber Eats 则采用了一套粗糙却低效的系统：配送无人机降落在配送司机的车顶，然后由司机把食物走到客户门口。不过，大多数针对“最后一英尺”问题的解决方案都倾向于同一种方法。

cues.en: Wing, SkyDrop, Flytrex, Wingcopter, and others have developed systems where their drones hover above the destination at a safe height and lower their payloads to the ground using cordsfar

cues.en: people, it turns out, are simply okay with waiting a day or two for their packages, while all want them delivered as quickly and cheaply as possible. When the drone delivery hype hit fewer pitch, one bit of nuance went overlooked:
cues.zh: 大多数人其实并不介意包裹等上一两天，他们只希望送得越快越便宜越好。当无人机配送的热潮渐退，有一点细微之处被忽略了：

cues.en: consumers simply don't care about how a package gets from B to C, so long as it's quick, cost efficient, and reliablethey'd
cues.zh: 消费者根本不在乎包裹如何从B点送到C点，只要快、省钱、可靠就行——他们

cues.en: opt for a new technology once for the novelty, but by the hundredth time, that wears off. Eventually, rationality will return. In fact, when surveyed in 2020, consumers perceived drones to potentially threaten those most important factors for them. They said they were uncertain about drones' reliability,
cues.zh: 会为了新鲜感尝试一次新技术，但到第一百次时，新鲜感就没了。最终，理性会回归。事实上，2020年的一项调查显示，消费者认为无人机可能威胁到对他们最重要的那些因素。他们表示不确定无人机的可靠性、

cues.en: cost, and were worried about the job loss they could incite. Meanwhile, competitors have figured out a number of low tech solutions that fulfill these consumer desires.
cues.zh: 成本，并担心它可能引发的失业。与此同时，竞争对手已经想出了不少低技术方案来满足消费者的这些需求。

cues.en: Look no further than food delivery apps. Since 2017the
cues.zh: 看看外卖应用就知道了。自2017年

cues.en: very moment when drone delivery hype hit fever pitchthe food delivery industry has tripled in size, ballooning into a $150,000,000,000
cues.zh: 无人机配送炒作达到顶峰的那一刻起，外卖行业的规模已经增长了两倍，膨胀成一个全球1500亿美元的

cues.en: sector globally.
cues.zh: 产业。

cues.en: In this, speed matters, and consumers expect to pay for the delivery costfacts
cues.zh: 在这方面，速度至关重要，消费者期望为配送成本买单，这些事实

cues.en: that seemingly pave a lane for drone delivery. But between Uber Eats, Grubhub, and DoorDash, the power players are already established, and the competition is already fierce.
cues.zh: 似乎为无人机配送铺平了道路。但在Uber Eats、Grubhub和DoorDash之间，巨头们已经站稳脚跟，竞争也已十分激烈。

cues.en: These comparatively low tech companies don't even tell the consumer whether to expect their burger to come by car, moped, bike, or footthey just prioritize getting food to doors quickly, pleasing the consumer regardless of method, and undercutting drone delivery in process. By and large, food delivery apps closely match the upside of drones within urban and suburban areas, without the hassle of complying with FAA guidelines and figuring out the last foot problem. Adding to the competitive problems facing drone startups, these companies and others have since expanded into grocery, medicine, and goods deliveries.
cues.zh: 这些技术含量相对较低的公司甚至不告诉消费者他们的汉堡是通过汽车、电动车、自行车还是步行送达的——他们只优先考虑快速把食物送到门口，无论用什么方式都让消费者满意，并在此过程中压低了无人机配送的竞争力。总的来说，外卖应用在城市和郊区范围内已经很好地匹配了无人机的优势，而且无需应对FAA合规的麻烦和最后一英尺的难题。雪上加霜的是，这些公司和其他企业此后还扩展到了杂货、药品和商品配送领域。

cues.en: Put simply, from the consumer perspective,
cues.zh: 简单来说，从消费者的角度来看，

cues.en: the problem drone delivery was designed to address has already been solved without building out a massively complicated aerial delivery network. The current low tech gig economy model isn't perfect, thoughfor consumers and restaurants alike, the usage fees are expensive, for those delivering the pay is minimal, and for the big players, profit has proved elusive.
cues.zh: 无人机配送原本要解决的问题，已经在无需构建极其复杂的空中配送网络的情况下得到了解决。不过，当前的低技术零工经济模式并不完美——对消费者和餐厅来说，使用费用昂贵；对配送员来说，报酬微薄；对巨头们来说，盈利已被证明难以实现。

cues.en: One partial solution is automation.
cues.zh: 一个部分解决方案是自动化。

cues.en: Here still, though, drones are likely to lose out. Ground based autonomous and semi autonomous robotics have begun popping up in test markets, and partnering with the likes of Uber Eats and Grubhub to expand their reach. While a recent partial ban on sidewalk wandering robots in San Francisco points to the hurdles the technology faces, these hurdles just won't be as numerous as those facing drones.
cues.zh: 不过，无人机在这方面仍可能处于劣势。地面自主和半自主机器人已开始在测试市场崭露头角，并与Uber Eats和Grubhub等伙伴合作扩大覆盖范围。尽管旧金山最近部分禁止了人行道漫游机器人，这表明该技术面临障碍，但这些障碍不会像无人机面临的那么多。

cues.en: Automation and technological advances may well help smooth out food and last mile delivery. In the near future, your prescription,
cues.zh: 自动化与技术进步很可能有助于理顺食品配送和最后一公里配送。在不久的将来，你的处方药，

cues.en: your lunch order, or your afternoon coffee might be showing up your front door courtesy of an autonomous vehicleyou'll just need to reach down and grab it from a robot, instead of unclipping it from a drone above.
cues.zh: 你的午餐订单，或者下午的咖啡，可能会由自动驾驶汽车送到你家门口；你只需要弯腰从机器人那里取下来，而不是从头顶的无人机上解开取货。

cues.en: Now, many probably now look at drone delivery in retrospect, and find it unsurprising that the bombastic claims of the 2010s failed to pan out, but far fewer would have expressed a dissenting opinion just five years ago. That's because this is a rather classic storythat
cues.zh: 现在很多人回头看无人机配送，会觉得2010年代那些夸夸其谈没能兑现并不意外，但就在五年前，很少有人会公开表示异议。这是因为这是一个相当典型的故事——

cues.en: of a hype cycle. A new idea comes around, a few early players start development, then somethinga
